lineage_512_to_4096.finding: docs/decisions/0016-sampling-cap-change.md:6-20 — max_tokens 512 interacted with the subject model's reasoning tokens (billed against completion_tokens) to kill long call chains. Per call the at-cap risk was symmetric (2.41% vs 2.42%); per episode it fell 4.8:1 against the BASELINE, because a no-Skill episode takes ~10.9 calls against ~2.3 with the Skill. Three of six paid comparisons died this way; USD 0.5037 of certification spend bought no comparison.
lineage_512_to_4096.decision: docs/decisions/0016:22-49 — raise the cap identically on both variants, one symmetric change; new Campaign digest and full downstream cascade; post-change certification restarts; pre-change and post-change runs never share a stability set; every pre-change run becomes disclosed diagnostic evidence; programme cap rises USD 2.00 → 3.00.
lineage_512_to_4096.value_chosen: 4096, justified at tools/build_fixture_catalog.py:159-180: eight times the observed ceiling of an uninterrupted call (501 tokens) and eight times the worst observed reasoning burst (512); half of the harness's own max_output_tokens of 8000; the median call is 143 tokens and is unaffected.
lineage_512_to_4096.ratification: docs/decisions/0017-cap-ratification-and-freeze.md:8-15 — 0016 ratified; a changed scientific configuration creates a new artifact lineage and never retroactively repairs the old one. Amber item at :27-35: two individual baseline CALLS reached 4096 (longest 4098) and the harness recovered; no episode was killed post-change; the cap is not raised again.

The pinned Hermes harness may apply internal defaults for turns or episode duration. Techtree neither sets nor records them, and the pinned engine is not vendored in this repository, so whether any default bound exists behind the unset knobs was not established. This does not change the finding that the CAMPAIGN's declared timeout reaches nothing.

Decision 0017:92-101 requires the Gate-1 packet to carry a sampling-cap correction lineage section (old digest + 512, failure IDs/arms/costs, 0016, new digest + 4096, regeneration report, post-change canonical IDs) with two explicit statements. release/founder-skill-approval-draft.md contains no such section: it never states the pre-change campaign digest, never states 512 or 4096, and carries neither explicit statement. §4 classifies the runs pre/post change and §6 gives the incomplete-run cost, which covers part of the requirement. Reported as a finding for WP11h rather than fixed here.

enforcement_refresh_0029.limit_selection: release/limit-calibration.json — 731 successful canonical episodes, the predeclared formulas applied
enforcement_refresh_0029.summary: The 2026-08-14 audit found declared limits that limited nothing. Decision 0029 made every one of them real and regenerated the Campaign around what the measured episodes actually need. Every field this audit lists as declared is now carried to a place that enforces it, and the spending maximum is a precondition the run is refused on rather than a number on a screen. The two values that could not survive being enforced unchanged were changed by predeclared formula, not by judgement: the output ceiling, because a measured episode had already reached it, and the spending maximum, because the enforced token limits can amount to more than the old one.

every_declared_field_now_enforced.mechanism: src/techtree/verifiers/budget.py::require_cost_bound, called from src/techtree/runs/real.py:243-255 require_bounded_campaign at real.py:365 — after the credential check and before the first container. The most the comparison can cost under the enforced token limits is computed at the prices this release recorded, and a Campaign that could amount to more than it declares is refused with code campaign_cost_bound_exceeded.
every_declared_field_now_enforced.why_it_moved: The bound computed from the enforced limits is $2.42, which is above the old $1.00, so the old maximum would have refused the Campaign this build ships. Raising it is a new Campaign version, which is what this is. It remains a ceiling and not a price: every canonical comparison measured so far settled between $0.16 and $0.20.

every_declared_field_now_enforced.mechanism: src/techtree/verifiers/child.py:128 VARIANT_HARD_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 1800.0, passed to the child-local supervisor process that wraps each managed eval: hard monotonic deadline, SIGTERM to the eval's own process group then SIGKILL after a 20 s grace (inner grace < the outer 30 s, invariant-tested).
every_declared_field_now_enforced.margin: the longest measured variant took 1261.3 s, 70.1% of the deadline

every_declared_field_now_enforced.was: unbounded — a hard-killed worker left its evaluation children spending
every_declared_field_now_enforced.mechanism: parent-liveness pipe: the worker holds the write end, so its death (SIGKILL included) is EOF on the read end and the supervisor signals the eval group immediately. Reason recorded as parent_lost in the private 0600 supervision record (techtree.eval-supervision.v1).

cost_bound.formula: tasks x variants x ((I + C) x input_price + (O + S) x output_price) / 1e6
cost_bound.why_the_overshoot_terms: The pinned build checks its caps between turns, so the turn that crosses one still completes: at most a whole context window in and one sampled reply out. A bound that ignored that would be a figure that is usually right.
cost_bound.observed_actual_cost_per_comparison_usd: 0.16 to 0.20 across the canonical runs; the bound is deliberately pessimistic and is not an expected price
cost_bound.honest_form_of_the_claim: Token exposure is protocol-bounded; the dollar figure uses provider pricing recorded at release time.
